title: Orbit emission over a finite range
statement: Let $g$ and $\mathrm{out}$ be maps on finite bit strings, let $P,Q:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}^*$, and let $K,N$ be natural numbers with $K<N$. Suppose that for every $i\le K$, the $i$th iterate of $g$ from $s_0$ is the pair encoding of $P(i)$ and the pair encoding of the string of $K-i$ ones with $Q(i)$; suppose also that every iterate with index greater than $K$ equals the completed-block string, and that $P(i)$ is nonempty for all $i\le K$. Then concatenating the emissions at iterates indexed from $0$ through $N-1$ gives precisely $\mathrm{out}$ applied to the pair encoding of $P(K)$ and the pair encoding of the empty string with $Q(K)$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $i$ with $K<i$, $g^i(s_0)$ is the completed-block string
